title: Preflight signal playbook for LTS branch certification
creator: Aisha Bhatia
description: Goal: Create a reproducible, automated preflight 'signal playbook' that consolidates smoke probes, perf regression gates, and targeted eval suites to certify an LTS branch before internal release. The playbook should run as a single pipeline with clear pass/fail semantics, produce a human-readable report, and emit machine signals consumed by the rollout controller. Scope includes: defining canonical smoke probes for critical endpoints, a lightweight perf gate tailored to expected 99th/median latency budgets, and an evaluative quality suite for a small representative prompt corpus. Non-goals: full-scale benchmark sweeps across every model variant (this is a targeted preflight for branch certification).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CI pipeline that runs smoke tests, perf gates, and evals against the LTS candidate and outputs a consolidated JSON report.
Perf gate enforces 2% regression allowance on P50 and 5% on P99 compared to release-accepted baseline; failures flag the branch as 'Do Not Promote'.
Smoke probes cover 8 user-facing routes (generation, chat-streaming, embeddings, KV-heavy continuations) and must return correct status codes and basic output sanity checks within 5s.
Eval suite runs 200 curated prompts with automated quality heuristics and highlights any top-10 regressions for manual triage.
Signals are wired to the rollout controller (canary/abort) and surfaced in the release dashboard with links to failing traces and PRs.
Runbook documented in Confluence with post-mortem template and rollback playbook linked.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Aisha: Drafted initial playbook outline and mapped required probes to existing smoke tests (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Preflight+Playbook).

2026-03-01 - Ethan: Spike completed to run lightweight perf harness against runtime-2.0-lts on a c5g-like perf env; observed 1.8% median regression on kv-cache path. Decided to widen perf window to 2% but add a targeted kernel sampling check.

2026-03-03 - Eng review: Agreed to reuse the 'prefix-cache' synthetic workload from ENG-62321 and add an additional streaming stress probe for function-calling paths. Trade-off: increases CI runtime by ~12 minutes but improves signal for streaming regressions.
2026-03-06 - PM feedback (Nora Chen): Require explicit customer-impact tagging in reports; added 'customer-impact' field in consolidated JSON to call out high-risk failures.

2026-03-08 - Design (Maya Ortega): Reviewed report mockups; recommended single-pane failure summary with collapsible detailed traces. Added link to design spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PlaybookDesign
2026-03-10 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281 implementing perf gate comparator and JSON report exporter.
2026-03-12 - Infra (Kai Park): Provisioned a short-lived test pool for LTS preflight to avoid impacting prod capacity; config at https://repo.redwood.ai/infra/blob/main/preflight-pools.yaml
risks: False positives from flaky smoke probes causing unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by sample dedup/retries and a flakiness baseline collected over 72h.
CI runtime growth may slow release cadence — mitigation: parallelize eval shards and provide an opt-in fast path that runs lighter checks for hotfix branches.
Perf deltas confounded by noisy infra — mitigation: run baseline and candidate back-to-back on same ephemeral pool and capture CPU/GPU telemetry.
Undetected semantic regressions that quantitative heuristics miss — mitigation: mandatory manual review when top-10 eval regression KPI exceeds threshold.
Signal coupling with rollout controller needs hardening to avoid accidental aborts — include a dry-run mode and a manual confirm step for critical branches.
rollforward_plan: If preflight fails with clear perf regressions limited to a single kernel path, attempt a warm-cache rerun after candidate patch; if failures persist, revert to previous LTS commit and open a regression PR. For ambiguous eval regressions, tag triage leads and schedule a 2-hour investigation window before promoting. Document steps in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Preflight+Runbook
notes: We should keep a 30-day historical window of preflight signals for LTS branches to detect drift over time.
Consider exposing a lightweight 'preflight status' endpoint in the console microfrontend for on-demand checks by SREs.
Follow-up: automate annotating impacted customer workspaces when an LTS preflight flags a high-severity regression.
Incident learning: in 2025-11 a similar preflight missed a streaming regression due to small corpus; plan to expand streaming probes in the next iteration.
